<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.7.6/docs/squad-invite.gif" width="640" alt="Two boards side by side: BIGFOOT taps ADD TO SQUAD, YETI's board asks and accepts, both show the same four digits, the phrase goes over, and YETI is in without typing anything."></p>

**Two boards can now put a third in the squad without anyone typing five words into a payphone.** ADD TO SQUAD sits beside INVITE on the SQUAD screen. Pick a board in range, tap it, and their board asks them whether they want in. Both screens then show the same four digits, which the two of you compare out loud, and the phrase goes across sealed under a key that exists for that one exchange and no other. The four digits are the whole security of it: they come from both boards' keys, so a third board sitting in the middle pretending to be each of you to the other shows up as two screens that disagree. If the radio dance fails, the inviter's screen offers to show the phrase for typing instead, which is how it always worked and still the most reliable way in.

**Every board in range can be told to update at once.** UPDATE SQUAD, on the UPDATE FIRMWARE screen, tells every board with your phrase to install the version this one is running. Each of them shows a thirty-second countdown with a SKIP button, joins WiFi, installs the signed release from the site, restarts, and reports back by name to the board that asked. The sender can share its own saved network with the nudge, sealed with the phrase, and the receiving boards use it once and forget it. A board only listens if REMOTE UPDATE is on in its SECURITY screen, which it is not until you say so, and a locked board ignores the whole thing. That is what you get for locking. Tested on two boards up to the part where they report back, which needs a release newer than the one they're on, so this is the release that proves it next time.

**The light on the back of the board does something now.** A slow breathe in the theme's colour when nothing is happening, three flashes and a hold in the detection's own colour when something is, a double-blink for an unread message, a blip when a squad member walks on, cyan while an update downloads and green or red for how it went. STATUS LIGHT under APPEARANCE has the switches: alerts, messages, idle breathe or solid or off, an idle colour that can follow the theme or the background or be one of nine fixed ones, brightness in five steps, and a TEST row that plays the lot in six seconds. On the 2.8" CYD the light is on the back; on the RL Phantom it is on the front. It stays dark on the lock screen and through a wipe, so a duress restart looks like any restart from the back too.

**Getting this version:** from v1.7.4 or v1.7.5, UPDATE OVER WIFI or Bluetooth. From anything older, the USB flasher. Once one board has it, UPDATE SQUAD does the rest of yours.

## The phrase can be hidden

SHOW PHRASE, a row on the PHRASE screen, is on by default and does what every board did before. Off, the five words become dashes, the board never prints them anywhere, and the only way into the squad from that board's side is ADD TO SQUAD in person. Anyone who already knows the phrase can still type it into a board of their own; the switch stops this board from telling.

## Speech bubbles you can read

Squachy's quips, the visit dialogue, the red message bubble and the boot tagline are set in the display's medium font, about half again the size of the small one. Twelve fonts with more personality were converted and tried in its place, and every one of them looked converted rather than native at this size, so the plain one stayed. The converter is in the repo for anyone who wants to try their luck.

## Every menu under Settings looks like Settings

The power saver, status light, type filter, ignored devices, security and SquachMesh screens now have the same heading, the same panel rows in the colour of the row that opened them, and the same BACK strip pinned to the bottom. Two of them had no row panels at all before, so the synthwave sun came through the letters. Every menu row is two pixels taller for thumbs.

## Weekly updates

Five days, eleven releases, and this is where it ended up. For anyone who blinked:

- **v1.5.23, Wednesday.** SquachMesh: another SquachWatch in range walks onto your screen in its owner's outfit and the two Squachys talk.
- **v1.5.24, Thursday.** Messages between boards, encrypted with a five-word phrase, canned or typed on the payphone.
- **v1.6.0, Friday.** Thirty-five emotes, both Squachys acting them out together, and a roaming crowd of up to eight.
- **v1.7.0, Saturday.** Settings regrouped with fold-away headings and a SYSTEM page, a WATCH/HUNT badge, and a second firmware slot for updates to land in.
- **v1.7.2, Saturday.** Updates over WiFi straight from squachwatch.com and over Bluetooth from a browser, signed, with a thirty-second trial and automatic rollback.
- **v1.7.4, Sunday.** Bluetooth updates actually working, several times faster, plus hold NEARBY to open the closest device and a slimmer Squachy.
- **v1.7.5, Sunday.** The SD card boot loop fixed at its real cause, the RL Phantom logging to its card, and two emulator tests that render every screen in every theme and every outfit in every pose.
- **v1.7.6, Sunday night.** The status light, ADD TO SQUAD, UPDATE SQUAD, a hidden phrase, bigger bubbles, and matching menus. This one.

Also the owl and the lil guy say PCBWAY! now, because they were asked to.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: ADD TO SQUAD, an in-person invite with a four-digit compare, no typing
- **Added**: UPDATE SQUAD, one tap to update every board in range, with a countdown and SKIP on each
- **Added**: REMOTE UPDATE on the SECURITY screen, off by default
- **Added**: the status light, with its own screen under APPEARANCE
- **Added**: SHOW PHRASE on the PHRASE screen, for invite-only squads
- **Added**: the RL Phantom's front LED, same rules as the CYD's
- **Changed**: speech bubbles, visit dialogue and messages in the medium font
- **Changed**: every menu under Settings has a heading, panel rows and a pinned BACK
- **Changed**: menu rows are two pixels taller
- **Changed**: the owl and the lil guy have one more line
